evidence.eventual_fix_title: fix: conv2d_tiled produces wrong results when C == H == W
evidence.eventual_fix_problem_statement:
fix: conv2d_tiled produces wrong results when C == H == W

## Bug

`conv2d_tiled` produces **completely wrong output** when `C_in == H == W` (e.g., input shape `[1, 64, 64, 64]`).

Fixes #3404

## Root Cause

`conv2d_tiled` converts input from NCHW to NHWC internally. It uses a stride comparison to skip this conversion if the input appears to already be NHWC:

```rust
let layout_is_valid = inp_l.stride() == [H*W*C, W*C, C, 1];
```

**When `C == H == W`, NCHW and NHWC strides are numerically identical:**

| Layout | Strides |
|--------|---------|
| NCHW `[B, C, H, W]` | `[C*H*W, H*W, W, 1]` |
| NHWC `[B, H, W, C]` | `[H*W*C, W*C, C, 1]` |

When `C == H == W = 64`: both become `[262144, 4096, 64, 1]`. The check passes, conversion is skipped, and NCHW data is read as NHWC during im2col — producing completely wrong results.

## Fix

```rust
// Before:
let layout_is_valid = inp_l.stride() == [cont_s0, cont_s1, cont_s2, 1];

// After:
let layout_is_valid = false;
```

Candle tensors are always NCHW. The "already NHWC" fast path can never legitimately fire, so we disable it entirely.

This same fix is applied to both `conv2d_tiled` and `conv2d_direct` which share the same pattern.

## Correctness

Added regression test `conv2d_c_eq_h_eq_w` that:
- Creates `Conv2d(4, 2, 3x3, padding=1)` with input `[1, 4, 4, 4]` (C==H==W==4)
- Verifies output channels are identical for all-ones kernel (sanity check)
- Verifies specific output value matches hand-calculated expected result

**Without fix:** test fails (`got 4.232, expected 1.431, diff=2.80`)
**With fix:** test passes

All 8 existing conv tests continue to pass.

## Performance

The `layout_is_valid` optimization only fired when `C == H == W` — which is the case that produced wrong results. For all other inputs (the vast majority of real models), the conversion was already running.

| Case | Before | After | Impact |
|------|--------|-------|--------|
| `[1,64,64,64]→384` (bug case) | 8,716 us | 10,215 us | +17% (was producing wrong output) |
| `[1,128,56,56]→256` (general) | 8,487 us | 7,746 us | noise |
| `[1,256,28,28]→512` (general) | 8,379 us | 8,097 us | noise |
| `[1,512,14,14]→1024` (general) | 11,821 us | 11,204 us | noise |

**No correct computation becomes slower.** The bug case is slower because it now performs the (necessary) conversion, but the previous "fast" result was incorrect.

## Real-world Impact

This bug prevented correct inference of [BiRefNet](https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet) at 1024x1024 resolution. The model's decoder produces intermediate tensors of shape `[1, 64, 64, 64]`, triggering the bug. With this fix, BiRefNet inference matches PyTorch within fp32 precision at all resolutions.

- [candle-birefnet](https://github.com/developer0hye/candle-birefnet) — BiRefNet implementation that discovered this bug
